title: The Sigma3 normal form uses a Pi2 row relation.
details: Kelly, 13. Cubbyhole Mathematics, Proposition4, first displayed normal-form paragraph of the proof, checked2026-11-08. The proof says that a Sigma3 predicate P(x) is equivalent to exists y R(x,y) for a Sigma3 set R, then claims R(x,y) iff an associated c.e. domain is infinite. The intended row relation is Pi2: use P(x) iff exists y forall u exists v Q(x,y,u,v) with computable Q, and take R(x,y) to be the Pi2 inner condition. Pi2-completeness of INF then supplies the ordinary uniform row map on the paired parameter. Changing Sigma3 to Pi2 repairs this local normal-form slip; the later marker sketch has separately recorded issues. Current adoption2026-11-09: the REC construction uses a single paired Pi2 row relation and the earlier uniform INF reduction, before taking its outer existential.
